ce_bugs.text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28 — Changing GET /groups/:group_id/members from a top-level array to an object without versioning breaks existing clients that deserialize or iterate the response as an array.

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Applying a new default limit of 50 to every group silently changes non-automatic groups from returning all members to returning only the first page, so callers can unknowingly operate on incomplete membership data.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:24 — Removing the established nested group payload from POST /admin/groups makes existing callers submit an empty name and fail validation instead of creating the requested group.
app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:26 — Limiting every group to 50 members hides later members on the public members page because it has no pagination controls.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:25 — Fetching members by the editable unsaved group name makes pagination and membership refresh fail or display another group's users after a rename is typed.

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — The client-controlled limit has no upper bound, so a single members request can materialize and serialize an entire large group and exhaust application memory or worker time.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:11 — The fire-and-forget membership request bypasses route error handling, so a failed request completes navigation with an empty or stale members view.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:64 — The add-members action discards the mutation promise and provides no rejection handler, so server failures become unhandled rejections with no actionable feedback.

mrv_findings.text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:26 — [confidence 100; P1] `members = group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` now truncates every group's member list to 50 by default, while the public group-members route fetches once and its template exposes no pagination, making members beyond the first page inaccessible there.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — [confidence 100; P2] `return Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1;` invents an extra page whenever the positive member count is divisible by the page size, so a 50-member group enables Next into an empty second page.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38 — [confidence 100; P1] `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` replaces the former nested-payload and incremental-PATCH handling without compatibility or versioning, so previously supported `PATCH` requests with `changes: {add: ...}` now return success without changing membership and silently make the group invisible.

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28 — [confidence 100; P1] `render json: {` changes the existing members endpoint's top-level array into a `{members, meta}` object without a versioned endpoint or compatibility mechanism, breaking existing API consumers that iterate the previous response shape.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:31 — [confidence 75; P2] `self.setProperties({` unconditionally commits every asynchronous member response, so rapidly paging forward and backward can let an older response overwrite the latest requested page and can let a pre-removal response restore a deleted member in the displayed list.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — [confidence 100, P2] `return Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1;` misses the exact-page-size edge case, so a 50-member group reports two pages and enables navigation to an empty second page.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:6 — [confidence 100, P2] `{{#each m in members}}` renders only the newly limited 50-member response without any pagination controls or further-page loading in the public route, leaving members after the first 50 inaccessible for custom groups that previously displayed all members.

spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:107 — [confidence 100, P2] `group.users.count.should == 2` adds users only to an empty group, so the replacement test passes if the new incremental add endpoint replaces all existing memberships, whereas the removed incremental-add test seeded an existing member.

spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:129 — [confidence 100, P2] `group.users.count.should == 0` removes the group's only member, so the new removal test passes even if the endpoint deletes every membership instead of only the requested user; retain another member and assert its identity survives.
